Pakistan will not be too disappointed though. They have got the runs on the board and now, will look towards their bowlers to make consistent inroads. Babar Azam and Fawad Alam highlighted their fightback again, recovering from 22/3. And then today, when they were seemingly losing their way, Faheem Ashraf took them from 149/5 to 272. His 78 looked assured and compact, taking Pakistan out of trouble. But, they will feel that are 50 runs short.

End of a wonderful bowling performance from South Africa. Someone needed to light the flame for resurrection and that was done by Anrich Nortje. His 5-fer kept the Proteas in the hunt, not letting the game drift away. Maharaj supported him well, with 3 scalps. But overall, the entire bowling unit was economical. What reads 272, could well have been 300-plus had the brakes not been applied on the scoring.

We are all set to begin the second session of Day 2. The South African players are out in the middle. Yasir Shah and Faheem Ashraf will resume their innings for Pakistan. Wiaan Mulder will start the proceedings for this session.
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

Well, we have a long Lunch break, scheduled for an hour, due to today being a Friday and the players offering their prayers. The second session is scheduled at 1.30 pm local (0830 GMT). 60 overs left in the day. You too, take a break but please do return for what could be an entertaining second session. In the meanwhile, you can switch tabs and catch the action from the first India-England Test in Chennai.

Not a good batting session for Pakistan but full marks to Faheem Ashraf. He came in under pressure, soaked in all of it and has played a quality knock thus far. He has got to his half century and with not much batting left, will look to shepherd the tail and carry Pakistan as close to 300 as possible. That should be a good score on this deck.

Anrich Nortje struck early in the day, removing Babar Azam early. Fawad Alam then followed suit, getting run out, thanks to a piece of brilliance from Temba Bavuma. But what followed after that was a blockathon. Mohammad Rizwan simply could not get going and laboured to 18 from 68 balls. He was involved in a 41-run stand with Faheem Ashraf but while he did succeed in wearing out the bowlers, the scoreboard was not ticking along, which helped the Proteas to strike twice quickly again, towards the end of the session. Nortje and Maharaj have been the pick of the bowlers, sharing 3 apiece. And the good news for South Africa is that George Linde is back, so the load on Maharaj can be shared.

Phew. End of a longggggggg session. 165 minutes! Close to 3 hours. At the end of it, South Africa come out as the happier side. 84/4 in 38 overs shows the control with which they have bowled, reaping rewards with 4 wickets. They were lucky with a couple of those, with Azam and Alam gifting their wickets away but their bowling has been clinical.

Bull's eye! Fawad dives in but the Proteas celebrate. It is referred upstairs and replays confirm the worst for Alam. Both set batsmen gone! Coach Misbah-ul-Haq in the dressing room is not happy at all. Sensational fielding.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! That is a sharp catch from Faf but what a start for South Africa! They just could not have wished for anything better. Azam gone on the second ball of the day. The stand which was looking so threatening for the visitors has been broken. That is a loose, loose stroke from Azam. Yes, he was batting in his 70s but this is a new day and you need to be a little cautious especially at the start of a new day. It is a nothing delivery. It is short and wide outside off. Azam slashes at it away from the body. It flies off the outside edge towards second slip where Faf takes a good catch. Can South Africa now build on this one?

We are all set now for the action to begin! The Pakistan players make their way out to the middle. Fawad Alam and Babar Azam will resume their innings. It is going to be Anrich Nortje to start off proceedings today for South Africa. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Mike Haysman says it is very chilly out there! Aads it is a abrasive surface and there are a few cracks and they are going to open up more as the game progresses. Reckons it is going to be a good day of Test cricket.

Concerned about the weather? Yes, we know it spoiled the entire last session but things are looking bright and sunny for Friday. We will be having an early start and since it's Friday, we will have an extended morning session. So, stay tuned as we bring to you all the action.

Hello and welcome everyone for the second day of the second Test match in Rawalpindi. We witnessed some compelling cricket in the first two sessions were both teams had their say. South Africa enjoyed a great morning session by picking three wickets but as was the case in the Karachi Test, the home team bounced back through a century partnership which again involved Fawad Alam and this time he is partnered by skipper Babar Azam. They have led the recovery well and would be looking to extend the advantage today. Stay tuned for more.

Right! That's all from Day 1. Pakistan will be the happier side at the moment but South Africa will know that early strikes on Day 2 can turn things in their favor. Pakistan will want Babar and Fawad to get to the three-figure mark and put on a big first innings score. So, plenty to look for on Day 2. The action for the same will begin on Friday, 5th February 2021, at 0945 local (0445 GMT). Do join us for all the action. Until then, goodbye and take care!

South Africa started the Test match brightly. They didn't allow the Pakistani openers to get going. Maharaj struck twice in two overs for the Proteas to push the hosts under pressure. Nortje removed Abid Ali to force them further on the back foot. However, after that, the Protea bowlers failed to get past the association of Babar and Fawad. We couldn't get underway due to the rain and the entire last session was washed out.

Pakistan opted to bat first after winning the toss. Their openers did well to negate the first 10 overs of the morning but Pakistan lost three in quick succession. And after that, skipper Azam and Fawad took the control of the game. They managed to remain unscathed in the first session and played out the entire second session without any damage with the skipper getting to his half ton in the process.

Entire third session of the day has been washed off. We were set for an intense finish as we could've had plenty of drama in the last session of the day but with rain around, we have been deprived of that. However, we had a pretty good couple of sessions. The first one can be termed as shared one but the second session saw Pakistan dominate.

The visitors will hope that Linde does some magic if he returns and shares the workload with Maharaj. It is going to be an interesting session. Both the batters might want to get quick runs and that's when the South Africans might sense the chance to get an opening. Join us for the final session of Day 1 in a short while.

This has been a tough session for the Protea bowlers. There's hardly any assistance from the surface for them. And against two solid batsmen, they have failed to create opportunities. Maharaj has already bowled 25 overs and he must be surely missing Linde who didn't bowl in the entire session due to the injury in the first session. However, we might see him in action in the third session.

Babar has raked up his half ton and looking set for a big one. Fawad is not too far away from his half-century and he too will be eager to keep going along with the skipper. They have added 123 already and would look to make this into an even bigger stand. These two might look for some quick runs in the final session of the day and push the visitors further on the back foot.

A superb session for Pakistan. They have added 82 runs in this session in 29 overs and with a decent run rate as well. Babar is looking in classy touch while Fawad has been rock solid. Both the batters have not missed out on the scoring opportunities and have made this a very tough session for the Proteas.

Right then. Azam and Alam have done well to see off the bowlers until the first break but until when will they be able to do so? Can they come out and up the ante slightly to keep the scoreboard ticking or will they be on the defensive since they have lost three wickets? And will Maharaj inflict any more damage to the batting line-up of the Pakistanis? A lot of questions and all the answers will be found in the second session. Join us for that shortly.

South Africa started off well with the ball as Rabada and Nortje were making the ball talk and were bowling testing lines and lengths. But it was not until the inclusion of Maharaj, that they were able to pick at the wickets. He got got turn and bounce on this deck and he removed Butt and the experienced Azhar Ali too. Nortje then got rid of the other opener, Abid Ali. Rabada too has been bowling well but he has not been rewarded with a wicket yet. It will be interesting to see when Mulder will be introduced as well.

South Africa's session, you would say, based on the way things have flown by. But some good work by the skipper, Babar Azam and Fawad Alam has seen them build something after their poor start with the bat. The Pakistani openers started off nicely enough but when Maharaj was introduced into the attack, they did not know how to deal with him. First, Butt fell and then came Azhar Ali, who also could not deal with Maharaj and he fell for a 9-ball duck. Then it was Nortje's time to strike as a very good catch by Markram meant the end of the road for Abid Ali. Since then, Azam and Alam did well to see off the challenge until the Lunch break.

Flatter and around off, Fawad waits for it and then taps this one to the point region for one.
Loopy and on off, Alam works this one to the mid on region for one run.
Alam blocks this one nicely towards the off side.
Full and floated outside off, Alam pushes this one to covers. Says no for the single.
Tossed up and on middle, Azam whips this one through the mid-wicket region and the fielder does well to stop this one. Three runs taken.
Loopy and on middle, Azam keeps this one out.
Flighted on middle, pushed to the leg side.
On middle, pushed to mid on for no runs this time. A maiden for Linde.
Shortish and on middle, Fawad goes on his back foot and blocks again.
On middle, flicked to short leg.
On off, worked to the mid on region.
Down the leg side, Alam looks to sweep this one away to the leg side but he fails to get any bat on this one.
Flighted on off, Alam goes on the back foot to defend.
On middle, kept out.
Down the leg side, Azam misses his flick.

FOUR! A good stroke by the skipper there. Fetches a boundary. Loopy and on middle, Azam plays this with a straight bat through the mid on region, past the diving fielder there, into the ropes down the ground.
Flighted on middle, Azam tucks this one to square leg.
On middle, worked to mid-wicket.
Tossed up on off, Alam drives this one towards mid off for a single.
Floated on off, Azam keeps this one out.
On middle, Azam blocks it out.
Short, on middle, pulled to the square leg region for one.

An appeal for a catch taken but nothing from the umpire. Floated on middle and leg, Alam looks to work it to the leg side but he misses and the ball takes the pad and goes to the first slip where Bavuma takes it. But the umpire is unmoved. No bat on this one.
Blocked to the leg side again this time.
Tossed up on off, Alam tucks this to mid-wicket.
George Linde has the ball in his grasp now. Spin from both ends then.
Babar plays this one towards covers for no runs this time.
Flighted on off, Alam works this towards mid on for a quick single.
Flighted on leg, Babar tucks this to square leg for one.
On off, pushed to covers.
Flighted on middle, Azam blocks this towards square leg.
On middle, blocked.
Another bumper on middle, Alam looks to pull this one to the leg side but misses. A mild appeal for caught behind but nothing from the umpire.
Bowls an identical delivery to the last 2 balls again, Alam sits under this one again.
Bouncer again on the middle pole, Alam again sits under this one.
Bumper on middle, Alam ducks under this one.
Fawad Alam has just blocked that from his crease.
FOUR! Well played by Alam and he is off the mark as well. Fuller and on middle, Fawad flicks this one through the legs of the short leg fielder and into the deep square leg region for a boundary.
FOUR! Another one for the captain. Flighted on leg, Azam looks to block but the ball takes the inside edge and goes through the short fine leg region and the ball speeds away to the ropes.

FOUR! Azam is off the mark with a boundary now. Easy pickings for the skipper. Poor delivery this time. Short and wide outside off, Azam camps on his back foot and crunches this one through the cover region for a boundary.
On middle, kept out.
Tossed up and on middle, Azam blocks this with soft hands.
Flighted on off, Azam pushes this to silly point.
Flighted on leg, tucked to square leg.
Back of a length and around off, Alam hops and keeps it out. Another brilliant over by Nortje.
Who comes out now? The centurion of the last game, Fawad Alam is in.

OUT! TAKEN! What a catch by Markram by short leg. Reflexes had to really quick and Aiden has pulled off a stunner. Takes a one-hander as well. Abid Ali departs now and South Africa are on fire. Three quick wickets right in the first session. A back of a length delivery on middle, Ali hops and looks to tuck this one to the leg side. He does so and the ball goes to the right of the short leg fielder where Markram is stationed. He shows quick reflexes and moves to his right and pulls off a one-hand stunner. Another one falls and Pakistan are in a spot of bother now.
Outside off, left alone by Ali.
Length and around off, pushed to point by Abid.
Good length and outside off, Ali looks to block this one out but the ball zips away from the outside edge and goes to de Kock.
On a good length on off, Abid works this one to the off side. No Ball called for overstepping.
Outside off on a good length, Ali lets it be.
Flighted on off, Azam works this to covers again. Another wonderful over by Maharaj.
On off, pushed to covers.

Time for some DRINKS. Maharaj has been the trump card for the visitors as he has picked up 2 quick wickets and has pushed Pakistan on the back foot now. He is getting some good purchase on this deck and if he keeps going this way, then it will be tough for the hosts. Pakistan will be hoping to not lose any more wickets before the Lunch break. Also, the Pakistani skipper, Babar Azam makes his way out into the middle now.

OUT! LBW! Azhar Ali goes back now for a duck and Maharaj is on fire. The decision to bring him on very early in the innings is turning out to be a masterstroke by de Kock. Keshav floats one up nicely and lands it around off and middle, Azhar Ali comes on his front foot and looks to fend this one out but is not able to do so. The ball raps him on the pads. The South African players appeal loudly and the umpire obliges raising his finger. Azhar Ali looks at his partner, does not seem too convinced that the review will save him and then just turns around and walks off. Double blow for the hosts now.
On off, worked to covers.
Floated and on off, Azhar eases this one to mid off.
Shortish and around off, Azhar pushes this to point.
Abid Ali has just blocked that from his crease.
Goes on his back foot and blocks.
Outside off, Abid offers no shot to this one.
Drags his length back and bowls a bumper outside off, Abid sways away from the line of the ball and lets it through.
Around off on a good length, Abid again keeps it out.
Good length and on off, Abid blocks solidly.
On off, tapped to silly point. A wicket-maiden for Maharaj.
Tossed up and on off, Azhar pushes this one to covers.
On off, pushed to the off side.
Goes on his back foot and keeps this one out, does Azhar.
Floated on off, Azhar Ali pushes this one to the cover region.
Who's in at Number 3? Azhar Ali is in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Maharaj has struck and Butt does not survive this one. Great bowling by Maharaj and he breaks this opening stand. He has looked good so far and now he is rewarded with a wicket. Flighted and around off, spins away after hitting the deck as Butt comes forward looking for the defensive push. He is not able to do so and only induces a thin outside edge. It goes towards de Kock who does not miss out. An appeal and the umpire agrees raising his finger.
PLAY AND A MISS! On a good length and outside off, Ali slashes at this one but the ball misses the outside edge and goes to the keeper.
On middle, worked to mid on.
Short of a length again and outside off, comes back in after hitting the deck, Ali is about to leave this one but the ball takes the gloves and goes to the keeper on the bounce.
Back of a length and on off, Ali pushes this one to the cover region.
Outside off, left alone.

Another shout for lbw but Aleem Dar shakes his head. A length ball on middle and leg, Ali looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads. A loud appeal but nothing from the umpire. De Kock just turns around and goes back to take his position, does not seem interested in taking the review.
Tossed up and around off, Imran again, prods forward to defend. A good, testing over by Maharaj comes to an end.
Another block offered to this ball by Butt.
Tossed up and around off, IB works this to the off side.
On off, played towards mid off.
Comes forward and offers a solid defense to this one.
Flighted on off, Butt pushes this to short cover.
Fuller and on the pads, clipped to the leg side for a single.
Outside off, left alone.
Back of a length and around off, Butt gets his bat across and keeps this one out.
Butt blocks this one out solidly.
In the channel outside off, Imran leaves it alone.
Good length and on middle, Butt blocks this one out solidly.
Tossed up and outside off, Abid just lets this one through to de Kock.
Ali pushes this one to the cover region.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Floated outside off, Ali covers his off pole and leaves it alone.
On off, played back to the right of Maharaj.

EDGY...DROPPED! A regulation catch and Bavuma has let this one through the hands. A very poor effort. Flighted around off, spins away after hitting the deck, Butt comes forward looking to block this one but the ball kisses the outside edge and goes towards the first slip fielder where Bavuma does not grab this one. Just a single in the end.
Time for some spin as Keshav Maharaj is in to bowl now.
Ali offers a solid defense to this one. 2 runs off this over.
Fuller and on middle, Butt works this to square leg for one run. Ali wants the second but sees the fielder has already reached the ball and does not go for it.
Back of a length and around off, IB jumps and blocks this one.
Imran Butt has just watchfully blocked this out.
Butt comes forward and plays the off drive but it is a dot ball as the ball goes back to Rabada.
Bowls a fuller one on the pads, Ali flicks this one to the fine leg region for a single.
Butt was watchfully blocked this one out.
Butt defends this good length delivery with a very solid defense.
On middle, blocked to the leg side.
FOUR! Played it with soft hands and fetches a boundary for himself. On a length and around off, Butt guides this one through the gully region into the third man fence.
In the channel of uncertainty outside the off pole, Butt raises his blade to let this one through to de Kock.
Back of a length and on middle, clipped to the fielder at square leg.
On off, Abid keeps it out.
Abid Ali has just watchfully blocked this out.

EDGY FOUR! Lucky boundary and a lucky escape for Ali. On a length and around off, Abid is in two minds, whether to leave this one or to attempt this one, in the end, he lets his bat hang and the ball takes the inside edge and goes past de Kock into the fine leg fence.
A back of a length ball outside off, Ali shoulders arms this time around.
Pushes this one to the cover region.
Fuller and outside off, moving away from the right-hander, Ali leaves it alone.

Is Abid reading our commentary? Because he has opened his account right after we spoke about how he is yet to do that. But jokes apart, Abid scores his first run of the morning. A good length ball on middle, clipped to fine leg for a single.
On a good length and outside off, Abid lets this one through as well. Yet to open his account in this game, is Abid.
On a length and around off, Abid pushes this one to the off side.
Another length delivery outside off, Ali leaves this one alone again and de Kock collects.
Good length and on middle, tucked to the mid-wicket region.
Outside off, left alone.
Butt plays this good length ball to the point region this time. A maiden by Rabada.
Good length and on off, Butt looks to push this one away but the ball takes the inside edge and hits him on the pads.
Outside off on a good length, Butt shoulders arms to this one.
On a good length and around the off pole, Butt pushes this one to the cover region.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.

Another appeal for lbw but nothing from the umpire. A back of a length and on middle and leg, Butt misses his flick to the leg side and gets rapped on the pads. An appeal but nothing says the umpire. Was going down leg again.
Outside off, Abid does not want to have a poke at this one.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.

An appeal for lbw but turned down. A back of a length ball on off, nips into the right-hander and raps him around middle and leg as Ali misses his stroke. A loud enquiry but the umpire is not interested. Probably was going down the leg side.
Back of a length ball and around off, Ali blocks this one out.
In the channel outside off again, left alone.
Good length ball outside off, Ali leaves it alone.
Who will bowl from the other end? Anrich Nortje, it is.

EDGY FOUR! Edgy...but through the slip region. So close to getting the first breakthrough. On a length and around off, Butt looks to drive this one through the cover region and the ball takes the outside edge and goes in between the slip region and the gully region, into the third man region for a boundary. 8 runs off the first over.
In that channel outside off, Butt lets this one through to the keeper.
Another good length ball on off, Butt pushes this one to the cover region.
Length and outside off, left alone by Imran.

FOUR! Glorious way to begin your innings. What a wonderful drive. On a good length and outside off, some away movement noticed, Butt leans into this one and creams his drive through the cover region and into the ropes.
Rabada starts off with a good length delivery outside off, Butt shoulders arms to this one.

Right then. We are all in readiness for play to begin as all the pre-match formalities have been completed. The South African players are out in a huddle and after done they are done with their talk, they make their way and look to spread out on the field. The openers for Pakistan, Imran Butt and Abid Ali follow them out. Kagiso Rabada to begin proceedings with the ball for the visitors. Here he comes...

PITCH REPORT - Wasim Akram and Bazid Khan are out in the middle for the pitch report. Wasim says that there is little bit of grass and the deck is rock hard and there is some moisture on the deck as well. Feels that there will be some movement early on. Adds that the new ball will carry. States that he would have chosen to bat if he won the toss first.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Dean Elgar, Aiden Markram, Rassie van der Dussen, Faf du Plessis, Quinton de Kock (C/WK), Temba Bavuma, Wiaan Mulder (IN PLACE OF LUNGI NGIDI), George Linde, Keshav Maharaj, Kagiso Rabada, Anrich Nortje.
Pakistan (Unchanged Playing XI) - Imran Butt, Abid Ali, Azhar Ali, Babar Azam (C), Fawad Alam, Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Faheem Ashraf, Hasan Ali, Yasir Shah, Nauman Ali, Shaheen Afridi.
TOSS - Up goes the coin and it lands in the favour of Babar Azam. PAKISTAN WILL BAT FIRST!

Hello and a warm welcome to the second and final Test between Pakistan and South Africa which will be contested in Rawalpindi. After clinching the first Test convincingly, Pakistan will be hoping to complete a whitewash and will want to win this Test series 2-0. But it is not going to be an easy task by any stretch of the imagination as South Africa is not a team which just raises the white flag and gives up. They showed glimpses of what the talent that they possess and what they are capable of doing in the first game and if they come into this game with the same mentality, we are in for a cracker of a game. The Saffas will be looking to avoid a whitewash and will want to level things in the series as well. Will they be able to do so? Join us as we bring you the toss and the team news.
